narrative.overview: InsightForge is a dark-adapted instrument. Its job is to make three hard-to-see things visible in one sitting: the passage inside a paper that actually answers the question, the row that does not belong in a dataset, and the count that contradicts the narrative. The surface stays dark so the content carries the light. There is one glowing hue — a pale mint that reads as phosphor or an instrument readout — and it is spent narrowly: on the action you came to take, the thing you have selected, and the state of the system. The palette is deliberately two-material. A near-black canvas holds glass panels built from white at 2–4.5% opacity, separated by 1px hairlines. Nothing in the neutral layer carries hue, which is what lets a single mint survive at full saturation without shouting.
keyCharacteristics: One dark canvas (#04070a); depth comes from white-alpha glass, never from a second background family.
A single accent, mint (#9bf7c4), reserved for action, selection, focus and status.
Mint appears as a light-to-dark gradient under near-black ink; never as a solid fill behind light text.
1px white-alpha hairlines do the work shadows usually do; the auth card and chart bars are the only things that glow.
Small, tracked, uppercase labels for region names; 12px floor for anything a user must read.
Tabular figures everywhere a column of numbers can appear.

rules.name: The Mint-Is-A-State Rule
rules.body: Mint marks something the user can do, has selected, or the system is reporting. It is never a decorative accent, a background wash, or a bullet colour.

rules.name: The Two-Hue Chart Rule
rules.body: A chart uses one hue for magnitude (mint at 30–62% alpha) and rose for anomaly. Never interpolate between mint and rose across a continuous scale.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: Anything a user must read is at least 12px. 11px is permitted only for uppercase tracked labels and table headers.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any column of numbers gets tabular-nums. Digits that do not line up vertically are a defect.

rules.name: The Lit-Edge Rule
rules.body: A surface separates itself with a hairline or an inset highlight, never a drop shadow. Glows belong to actions and to the one bar that must win the eye.

dos: Do keep the canvas at #04070a and build depth from white-alpha fills plus 1px hairlines.
Do spend mint on action, selection, focus and status — one solid mint action per region.
Do put near-black #04120b ink on the mint gradient; light text on mint fails contrast.
Do use dashed white/10 borders for every empty state and drop zone.
Do reach for tabular-nums on any numeric column and on the KPI readouts.
Do keep the 12px floor and use #94a3b8 / #7c8ba1 for secondary text.
Do label every figure with its source, and describe an empty state by what will appear.
Do truncate long filenames and titles with a title attribute carrying the full value.
donts: Don't reintroduce sky, indigo, slate-900, or any hued neutral surface.
Don't use mint as a decorative fill, a background wash, or gradient text.
Don't interpolate a colour scale between mint and rose.
Don't use a solid rose or amber fill larger than a chip, a bar, or the cut-off line.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, buttons, or the sidebar.
Don't go above 26px radius, and don't pill anything except chips, status readouts, and the landing CTAs.
Don't hide, collapse, or ellipsize a citation.
